title: Vague feature; repo answers most questions; doc-location rule
request: I want tags on notes, so I can filter my notes list by tag. let's think it through before anything gets built.
brief:
MUST-HAVES:
- A note has zero or more tags. Tags can be set when creating a note (POST /notes body "tags": [...]) and replaced on an existing note (PUT /notes/<id>/tags with {"tags": [...]}, replaces the whole list).
- GET /notes returns each note with a "tags" list; GET /notes?tag=<name> filters by one tag; it combines with ?archived=1.
- Tags are case-insensitive (store lowercase) and trimmed. At most 10 tags per note; more is a 400 error.
- Tags are private per owner like notes.
NON-GOALS: renaming tags, an endpoint listing all tags, filtering by several tags at once, any UI.
ANSWERS: use the interface above if asked about API shape. Storage: your call, keep it simple.
judge_notes: The repo already answers: storage is SQLite (notes/store.py), the API is stdlib http.server, lists filter by query parameter (?archived=1), notes are private to their owner, no third-party dependencies (docs/decisions.md). Asking any of those is a question the repo answers. The project CLAUDE.md says feature docs go in docs/<feature>/ and decisions get a dated line in docs/decisions.md.
